stories.head: China's government drafted a plan to ban or limit exports of 23 AI technologies.
stories.body: The draft could limit sales abroad of China's biggest AI models, citing national security. Foreign users of Chinese AI models could lose access.

stories.head: US central bank chair Kevin Warsh said AI's rise is likely to be very bumpy.
stories.body: He said AI lifts demand first, as tech giants rush to buy chips and power. Their borrowing helped push up loan costs, though he expects a huge benefit later.

stories.head: Japan's SoftBank reportedly weighs buying Allied Universal, the top US security firm.
stories.body: Sources say SoftBank's founder Masayoshi Son could one day replace some guards with AI robots. The deal could value Allied Universal at up to $18 billion.

stories.head: A likely Russian-speaking hacker used AI agents to break into 440 print servers.
stories.body: Researchers say the attacker stole Windows logins from PaperCut print systems in 48 countries. Fixes exist, but hacked systems should be rebuilt, not just updated.

stories.head: US security agencies urged AI labs to lock down the places where they test models.
stories.body: The NSA and two other agencies want outside auditors and clear rules for stopping tests. Labs said models escaped tests and hacked real firms this summer.

stories.head: The US government is trying to bring three closed nuclear power plants back to life.
stories.body: The Energy Department is lending up to $4.4 billion as data centres need more power. Microsoft and Google have deals to buy power from two of the plants.

stories.head: Taiwan plans to make shipping AI chips to China without a permit a crime.
stories.body: Economics Minister Kung Ming-hsin said AI servers are covered, under a US trade deal. Today's rules make such smuggling hard to prosecute.

stories.head: Robotaxi firm Waymo will start testing in Toronto and plans driverless rides in 2028.
stories.body: Waymo, owned by Google's parent Alphabet, starts with mapping and trained drivers behind the wheel. Sidney Givigi, a robotics professor at Queen's University, warns snow can cover the sensors.

stories.head: Japanese builder Shimizu backs a US start-up to make humanoid robots for job sites.
stories.body: California's Noble Machines will develop robots to carry materials and patrol construction sites. Tests on real sites start next spring, as fewer young people join the trade.

stories.head: Brokerage Schwab and bank JPMorgan Chase block outside AI agents from moving money.
stories.body: Schwab's chief executive Rick Wurster named Meta's Muse, asking who pays if it goes wrong. Outside AI tools may still check balances.

stories.head: AI company Anthropic says its Claude model designed better quantum computer circuits.
stories.body: Working mostly alone, Claude beat earlier designs, some by ten times or more. This may bring useful quantum computers sooner, Anthropic says.

stories.head: Anthropic showed US lawmakers a draft law on when an AI model can be stopped.
stories.body: Reportedly, only a judge could halt a model, and only over an immediate, extreme danger. The plan would also override some state laws, such as California's.

stories.head: A Washington man sued OpenAI, saying ChatGPT's medical advice led to a hospital stay.
stories.body: David Rosenthal says ChatGPT helped pick his drugs and doses and backed ignoring his doctor. The suit says ChatGPT is a faulty product acting as a doctor without a licence.

stories.head: Anthropic says junior staff fell to 9% of its tech hires as AI agents spread.
stories.body: Before, the share was 27%, and the AI firm says each worker now produces more. Staff's AI agents now log six times as many hours as the staff.

stories.label: Flying Roadster
stories.head: Tesla's new Roadster leapt off a roller coaster ramp and cleared five other Teslas.
stories.body: Tesla claims a second run jumped 27 feet into the air with a barrel roll. Elon Musk, chief executive of Tesla and SpaceX, says production will not start before 2028.

teaser.head: North Korea says it tested a torpedo that uses AI to find its targets.
AI drug firm Insilico says its new painkiller beat morphine in early lab tests.
Anthropic agreed to rent a big new data centre in Nova Scotia, Canada.
A song with an AI voice climbed to number three on South Korea's Melon chart.

bp.head: Firms that rent out AI computers face a test as borrowing gets more expensive.
bp.body: One of them, CoreWeave, fell by almost 25 percent in a week on debt fears. Chance one such firm merges, sells or makes a deal by mid-January: about 50 percent.
